ops_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the setup of our team wiki workspace in {{vendor}}, our chosen project-management/docs tool. This requires my explicit sign-off before anything is finalized, so your job is to prepare everything and then stop.

First, ask me for any missing inputs you need:
- The workspace name and intended URL/subdomain
- The team or company name to use in branding
- Which sections we need (e.g., meeting notes, process templates, project docs)
- My preference on plan tier and access policy (who can join/edit/view)

Then do the following:
1. Using your configured credentials, walk through {{vendor}}'s guided first-time workspace setup flow as far as it allows without finalizing billing or ownership.
2. Draft the initial workspace structure: propose page/section hierarchy for meeting notes and process templates, and identify any pre-built templates in {{vendor}} that fit our needs (e.g., meeting notes template, project kickoff template, process/SOP template).
3. Prepare a customization plan for fields/workflow statuses that match our team's process, based on what I've told you.
4. Compile a checklist covering: proposed workspace name, plan tier, access/permission settings, initial page structure, and templates to import.
5. Do NOT create the final workspace, select a billing plan, invite members, or set ownership/access policy — these require my explicit approval.

When finished, report back with: the proposed workspace structure and template list, the plan tier and access policy recommendation, any setup steps you were able to complete via the guided walkthrough, and the full checklist awaiting my review. Clearly state that you have prepared everything but the workspace creation and access/ownership settings must stop for human sign-off before you proceed further.

ops_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the initial wiki structure for our team in {{vendor}}, our project-management tool, as part of setting up a team wiki (meeting notes + process templates).

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already clear, such as: the {{vendor}} workspace URL, the team or department name, the list of top-level sections we want (e.g. Meeting Notes, Process Templates, Team Directory, Onboarding), and any existing page naming conventions.

Using my configured credentials, draft (but do NOT create/apply yet):
1. A proposed page hierarchy for the wiki, with a home/landing page and clearly named sub-pages for meeting notes and process templates.
2. A proposed database structure for meeting notes (e.g. fields like Date, Attendees, Topic, Action Items) and one for process templates (e.g. fields like Process Name, Owner, Last Updated, Status), described as I could review and adjust.
3. A short outline of how these pages and databases would link together (e.g. meeting notes database embedded under its section page).

Present this full plan to me as a written draft — page titles, hierarchy, and database schemas — in a clear, reviewable format (e.g. a markdown outline or table). Do not create any pages or databases in {{vendor}} yet, since a human must explicitly approve the plan before any changes are applied.

When the draft is ready, stop for human sign-off: clearly state that you are pausing and waiting for my explicit approval before creating anything. Report back with the full proposed structure, any open questions or assumptions you made, and a note confirming no changes have been applied to the workspace yet.

ops_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up the Meeting Notes database in our team wiki, hosted in {{vendor}}. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) the workspace/site URL for our {{vendor}} instance, (2) the parent page or space where the wiki lives (or confirm you should create one called "Team Wiki" if none exists), and (3) our team's typical meeting types (e.g., standup, planning, retro, 1:1) so the fields match how we actually work.

Using your configured credentials, please:
1. Create a new database/table named "Meeting Notes" nested under our team wiki page.
2. Add fields/properties for: Meeting Title, Date, Meeting Type (select/dropdown with the meeting types I gave you), Attendees, Status (e.g., Scheduled, Notes Pending, Complete), Action Items, and a Notes/body field for free-form content.
3. Set up at least one default view (e.g., grouped by Meeting Type or sorted by Date descending) so entries are easy to scan.
4. Add one sample entry as a template/example showing how a real meeting note should look, so the format is clear to teammates.
5. Link this database from the main wiki landing page if one exists, so it's discoverable.

Done looks like: a working Meeting Notes database inside our {{vendor}} wiki, with the fields above configured, at least one view set up, and a sample entry demonstrating usage — all created directly in the tool via your credentials, no manual copy-paste needed from me.

When finished, report back: the URL/location of the new database, the field names and types you configured, the view(s) you created, and a short note on the sample entry so I can confirm it matches our workflow.

ops_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me complete step ops_003:n4 of our 'Set up a team wiki' process: creating process templates in {{vendor}}, our project-management tool of choice, as part of our canonical wiki setup.

First, confirm you have access to my {{vendor}} workspace using my configured credentials. If you need the workspace name/domain or the parent page where templates should live, ask me for it before proceeding.

Goal: Build a small library of reusable process templates inside {{vendor}} so team members can jumpstart new projects and keep shared docs/notes organized alongside their work.

Actions to take:
1. Create a top-level page (using the create-page API) titled 'Process Templates' to act as the home for this library, nested under our wiki's parent page.
2. Create a database (using the create-database API) to structure repeatable templates, with properties for Template Name, Category (e.g., Meeting Notes, Project Kickoff, Retrospective, Bug Report), Owner, and Last Updated.
3. Populate the database with at least 3-4 starter template entries covering common recurring processes (e.g., weekly meeting notes, project kickoff checklist, retrospective format, decision log), each linked to its own page with placeholder headings/sections a user would fill in.
4. Ensure each template page has a clear structure (headings, bullet placeholders) so it's genuinely reusable, not blank.
5. Link the 'Process Templates' page from the main wiki home page if one already exists.

Done looks like: a 'Process Templates' page exists, containing a database of at least 3-4 populated, well-structured template pages, all accessible from the wiki's main navigation.

Report back with: the page/database titles created, links (or IDs) to each, and a short list of the templates included, plus any access or permission issues you encountered.

ops_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me complete the 'Share with team' step of setting up our team wiki in {{vendor}}. The wiki (meeting notes and process templates) already exists; now I need it shared with the right people using proper permissions.

Please ask me for anything you need that isn't already available via my configured credentials, such as: the wiki workspace/site name in {{vendor}}, the list of team members (with emails) and the role each should have (e.g., full editor, commenter, viewer), and whether any sub-teams need private, restricted-access sections (e.g., a leadership-only or engineering-only area).

With that information, prepare (but do not apply) a complete sharing plan:
1. A list of each team member paired with the exact permission level/role you propose for them in {{vendor}}.
2. A proposal for any private sub-teams or restricted groups, including which members belong to each and what access they should have to specific pages or sections.
3. A short summary of how this structure maps to our meeting notes and process templates (e.g., who can edit templates vs. who can only view meeting notes).

Draft this as a clear, reviewable checklist or table so I can see exactly who gets what access before anything changes. Do not invite anyone, change any permissions, or create any sub-teams yet — this step requires a human to explicitly approve the plan before changes are applied. Once your draft is ready, present it to me and stop for human sign-off. Report back with the full proposed sharing/permissions plan and a note confirming you have taken no action in {{vendor}} yet, pending my approval.
